arguments.need: I use AI coding assistants like Claude Code and OpenCode, and I'm tired of re-explaining my project decisions and preferences every session. I want a command-line tool where the agent can save short notes and later pull them back with a search that understands meaning, not just exact keywords. All the embedding and model work has to happen on my own machine with no cloud API or account needed. It would also help if I could back up my notes to a JSONL file and restore them later.

picks.name: Mnemoteca
picks.summary: Local CLI that stores short memories and retrieves them with hybrid search.
picks.fit: Mnemoteca is a local CLI for short memories with hybrid search plus JSONL export and import.

why.claim: It is a command-line tool for short memories with meaning-aware retrieval.
why.value: Local CLI that stores short memories and retrieves them with hybrid search.

why.claim: It can back up notes to JSONL.
It can restore notes from JSONL.
All work stays on the local machine.

tradeoffs: Local embedding and reranking plus JSONL export/import were listed as not checked on the card, so they were not verified working.
Needs Go 1.21+ toolchain and GCC on the machine.
Verified only as a function check on Linux, not as agent integration with Claude Code or OpenCode.
